messages:
carmen: starting a gradual enable for structured responses on the hosted API tomorrow morning. plan is: 5% global traffic + opt-in pilot tenants (2 customers). putting out the initial rollout plan here for quick checks. pls shout if any hard blockers, esp SDK/back-compat or infra limits. :wave:
ben: quick q — will client SDKs auto-switch behaviour or remain opt-in? we need to avoid changing defaults mid-release.
alice: client-sdk here — we will not flip defaults. plan is a minor release where the feature is behind so_sdk_structured_output=false by default. example config: ```js
const client = new Redwood({ enableStructuredOutput: true })
```
irina: infra note — do we have fallback routing if the new handler throws or latency spikes? suggest a circuit-breaker that routes to text-only model variant and increments a fallback metric so dashboard shows regression. also want a 30m observation window before increasing percentage.
carmen: @alice thanks. @irina yes — adding server-side fallback flag so_server_structured_fallback=true that triggers on error/latency. will add metric names: so.latency.p95 and so.errors.fallback_rate. 30m hold sounds good.
sam: QA — i'll run a short test matrix tomorrow: small prompts, long convo windows, and malformed JSON from functions. pls include a sample failing prompt if you have one. also need a canary tenant with higher quota to surface perf regressions.
ben: guardrails: rate-limits verif, token-cost regression, and end-to-end logs for one request id across routing. can we tag canary requests with header `x-so-canary: true`? makes tracing easier.
carmen: yes we will add the header. example rollout cli to enable for tenant: ```bash
redwood feature enable --tenant acme --flag so_experimental_structured --percent 100
```
deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: runtime/structured-output-handler -> canary group at 2025-11-02T09:00:00Z (ID: dep-7801). automated rollback on >=3% error rate within 10m.
irina: will the canary include both hosted and dedicated customers? mixing could hide infra-specific regressions. recommend separate small dedicated pool for the two pilot tenants.
carmen: agree — separate canaries for hosted vs dedicated. for dedicated pilots we'll target the two pilot customers only. hosted 5% global.
ben: one more — SDK surface: we should add a clear migration note in changelog about how structured responses may add required fields to outputs and recommend schema validation in clients.
alice: will add changelog + opt-in toggles in the SDK and a runtime warning log when structured responses are returned and SDK is still on legacy parsing.
sam: QA will create a checklist (perf, schema-mismatch, fallback correctness). aiming to validate within 48h of canary start.
carmen: thanks all. i'll update the rollout doc and post the link here when ready. tagging infra & sdk owners in the doc. :rocket:
